name: comp-505

frames.best_why: Both halves used: day 26 circled and 10:30 filled white in the slot list.

tagline: Day calendar beside a scrolling column of bookable time slots.
summary: A bordered panel splits a month calendar from a narrow slot list. The right side names the chosen weekday and date above a scrollable stack of half-hour times, some greyed out, which fill white when picked.
appearance: A small black panel divided in two: on the left a month grid with weekday initials and white day numbers, on the right a column headed by a weekday and date, then six visible small outlined buttons stacked tight with a few dimmed.
behaviour: Pressing a day circles it white, updates the weekday heading and clears any chosen time. Clicking an enabled slot fills it solid white while disabled slots stay dim and unclickable; the slot list itself scrolls.
demo_content: November 2026 with day 26 and 10:30 picked; half-hour slots from 09:00, several greyed out.
search_phrases: pick an appointment date and time slot
calendar beside a list of times
choose a day then an hour
time slots greyed out when taken
scheduler for appointments on one day
date and slot selector side by side
book a meeting from a calendar list
use_when: Someone books a slot on a chosen day and taken times must look clearly unavailable.
avoid_when: The slot list is mock data that never changes with the day, so real availability means replacing the source.
customise: The eighteen time slots, their availability flags and the caption link are written in the file; real availability or a different date format means editing the source.
weight_why: One month grid and a short list of time buttons; nothing animates.

a11y.note: Days and slots are keyboard buttons with visible text, but disabled slots only dim and never say why they cannot be booked.

issues: Every date shows the same slots, so picking a new day leaves availability unchanged.
Only about six of the eighteen slots fit before the list must scroll.
The caption credits the calendar library instead of the picker.
polish_why: Crisp two-pane picker with clear slot states; a fixed slot list and cramped scrolling.
